subject: GreenStack onboarding: throughput acceptance roundtrip
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@greenstack.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <ops@greenstack.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GreenStack onboarding: initial throughput run results and next steps

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the runbook earlier. We kicked off a 30-minute throughput sweep this morning against the dedicated test pool you provisioned for us. Quick summary below:

- Peak concurrent requests: 320
- Average token/sec (per request): 18.4
- Median p50 latency (generation): 210ms
- p95 latency: 980ms (saw a tail spike around 09:03)

I attached the raw CSV export with per-request timestamps and counts (greenstack_throughput_v2.csv). Tom and I reviewed logs and suspect a short-lived queuing issue tied to how we batch requests in our client.

Our ask: can Redwood run your acceptance test (standard throughput acceptance profile) against our current payload set and confirm whether we meet the throughput target of 250 sustained concurrent QPS with p95 < 1s? If we fail, please provide the specific failure mode (queueing, GPU saturation, KV cache misses, etc.) and any recommended config tweaks.

We also flagged a couple of sample payloads that likely influence latency — I included a small sample file for your team to reproduce (attached).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Emma
Emma Li
Head of Platform Engineering, GreenStack AI

Attachments: greenstack_throughput_v2.csv

Subject: Re: GreenStack onboarding: initial throughput run results and next steps

Emma — thanks for the export and the clear ask. We pulled the CSV and scheduled an acceptance run for tomorrow morning with the standard acceptance profile you referenced. Immediate plan & owners: 

- Monica (CS) will own the acceptance checklist and sign-off criteria; she will confirm the exact test window and observers.
- Karthik (Infra/serving) will run the test against your test pool and capture telem (GPU util, queue lengths, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates).
- Laura (PM) will coordinate any follow-ups and record decisions in the HubSpot deal.

We will run two passes:
1) Baseline pass using your payload set as-is (replicates your run).
2) Optimized pass applying recommended batching/concurrency settings and the lightweight prefix cache we discussed.

Deliverables from Redwood for each pass:
- Per-request latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99)
- Token throughput and effective tokens/sec
- Resource metrics (GPU util, memory, queue length)
- Failure modes and suggested mitigations (if any)

Can you confirm availability for a 45-minute observation window tomorrow, Tue 4 Aug, 09:00–09:45 PT? If that timing doesn't work, propose alternatives. We'll post results to the shared drive and ping the HubSpot record.

Irene
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Emma / Team — I'm locking in the acceptance checklist and observers. Quick summary of what I'll verify during the observation window: 

- Sustained concurrency test at target 250 concurrent QPS for minimum 10 minutes
- p95 latency target: < 1 second (generation only)
- No sustained queue length > 2x baseline for longer than 60s
- No error rate > 0.5% (5xx or model timeouts)

I uploaded the acceptance checklist and runbook to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/ONBOARD-GS-0421 (read only for your team). The checklist file is CS_onboard_checklist.pdf. Please ensure your client is pointed at the dedicated test endpoint and that the payload sample (gs_payload_sample.json) is representative of the production mix.

If we pass both baseline and optimized passes, Monica will record the sign-off in HubSpot and propose a rollout plan. If either fails, we'll provide specific remediation steps (e.g., recommended batch_size, concurrency ceiling, prefix cache warm-up, or a small model-variant fallback).

Thanks — see you at 09:00 PT.

— Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Emma Li <emma.li@greenstack.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GreenStack onboarding: initial throughput run results and next steps

Team — quick technical notes from the baseline pass we just completed (09:00–09:12 PT):

- Baseline result: matched GreenStack's earlier numbers for median latency but our p95 hit ~1.05s under identical client concurrency bursts (so narrowly over target).
- Observed failure mode: short-lived queueing when concurrent bursts exceed internal batching window (batch flush interval ~12ms). Queue length peaked ~3x baseline for ~45s, correlated with a GC spike in the client that caused uneven request arrival patterns.
- Kernel/GPU utilization: ~78% avg, peaks to ~92% during bursts; no OOMs.
- KV cache hit: 86% after priming; cold-starts accounted for ~12% of p95 spikes.

Immediate recommendations for the optimized pass: 
1) Increase server-side batching threshold to reduce variance (batch size target 64–80 for your payload mix).
2) Add a lightweight client-side jitter to smooth bursts (recommended jitter window 8–16ms) — avoids synchronized flushing.
3) Warm KV cache for the top 20% prefixes (we'll provide a warm-up script).

I've attached a small payload sample and the warm-up commands (gs_payload_sample.json). We'll run the optimized pass now and post artifact links.

— Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachment: gs_payload_sample.json

Thanks everyone — we reran with the client jitter and warmed the top prefixes. Results (summary):

- Sustained 250 concurrent QPS over 15 minutes
- p50: 190ms, p95: 880ms, p99: 1.25s
- No queue length sustained beyond 40s; peak GPU util stable at 88%
- Error rate: 0.12% (transient retryable timeouts from a narrow window at 09:21)

Attached: final CSV (greenstack_throughput_v2.csv) — looks good against the acceptance checklist. From our side we'll want Redwood sign-off to move this workload to a Dedicated reservation and schedule a small canary in production next week.

Emma
Head of Platform Engineering, GreenStack AI
